items.desired_outcome: SR-Mjolnir has dedicated bridge nodes for cloud telemetry: one node decodes approved raw CAN gateway frames into typed telemetry where appropriate, and one DDS-to-IoTCore bridge exports approved DDS topics to AWS IoT Core MQTT with bounded low-overhead behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation starts from a branch created off origin/ryan/feat/cmake_update/qnx_support

Before implementation, the current CAN gateway contract and CAN-facing nodes are read and summarized, including raw CAN DDS frame types, /can<bus>/from_can_bus, /can<bus>/to_can_bus, and current per-node CAN ID filtering

Before implementation, the ROS2-era EMBD-v2-HighLevel iotcore_bridge is read and only appropriate ideas are ported; ROS2-specific parameter/client behavior and checked-in certificate assumptions are not copied

The CAN-to-IoT node subscribes to approved /can<bus>/from_can_bus raw CAN DDS topics, filters by explicit CAN ID allowlist, unpacks 8-byte payloads through named functions such as unpack_0x200(), and emits typed structs or typed DDS telemetry topics with units and stale-data policy

Closed-control-system data such as IBSE or motor feedback is evaluated per signal: route through DDS first when local consumers, infotainment, diagnostics, control, recording, or reuse need it; otherwise document why a direct cloud-only path is acceptable
The DDS-to-IoTCore bridge subscribes only to an explicit allowlist of DDS telemetry/status topics and converts them to compact MQTT payloads for AWS IoT Core
High-rate telemetry defaults to best-effort/latest-value DDS reads, bounded queues, batching or downsampling, and AWS IoT MQTT QoS 0 unless the signal is an event/fault requiring QoS 1
Faults, alerts, and operator-relevant events have a separate mapping from high-rate numeric telemetry and may use QoS 1 with retry/backoff
The bridge does not publish raw high-rate telemetry into AWS Device Shadows; shadows are reserved for state/config handled by VSN-0011
MQTT endpoint, topic namespace, certificates, private keys, and AWS account details are supplied through deployment configuration and are not stored in the repository
Tests cover CAN ID filtering, unpack functions, typed telemetry conversion, DDS allowlist export, MQTT payload formation, queue overflow, reconnect/backoff, and shutdown
